bpc.hero.h1: An important piece of advice for piles patients
bpc.hero.lede: Fear of colonoscopy keeps people away from the doctor and pushes them towards pharmacy medicines — why that path is risky, in plain language.
bpc.intro.p1: As far as I know, many piles patients, out of fear of the colonoscopy test, do not go to the doctor and suffer with the disease, and secretly take medicines from the pharmacy. As a result, the disease…
bpc.intro.p2: The post is the clinic's direct advice written for its patients. Below, the points of that advice are explained further in simpler words.
bpc.h2.why: Why does the doctor advise colonoscopy?
bpc.why.p1: Bleeding from the back passage can have more than one cause — piles, a fissure, or some other problem inside the bowel. Which cause is actually at work cannot always be told from the outside. Colonoscopy helps find these causes — seeing where the bleeding is coming from and identifying polyps or other conditions in the bowel if they are present.
bpc.why.p2: That is why doctors sometimes advise this test before or during piles treatment — so that treatment does not continue while the real cause stays unidentified. Which patient needs which test is decided by the doctor.
bpc.h2.risk: The risk of treating yourself with pharmacy medicines
bpc.risk.p1: Taking medicines on your own from the pharmacy may ease the symptoms for a while — but it can keep the real cause of the disease hidden. Treatment that runs on without the cause being identified can keep the disease smouldering and delay the right treatment at the right time.
bpc.risk.p2: Besides this, side effects of medicines, or clashes with your other health conditions — none of these sums can be done by yourself. Whatever medicine you take, tell the doctor if symptoms last a long time.
bpc.routine.p1: The name alone raises many questions in many minds. There is no shame in being afraid — but hiding the fear and avoiding the test is the biggest risk of all. Colonoscopy is a common, routinely performed examination. Ask the doctor directly the questions that come to your mind:
bpc.routine.q1: What will the pain or discomfort during the test be like?
bpc.routine.q3: What happens before, during and after the test?
bpc.routine.p2: Fear eases a great deal once you have your answers and go ahead with the test. Asking questions and overcoming the fear is the easier path compared to enduring the discomfort for years.
bpc.h2.talk: What to discuss with the doctor
bpc.talk.1: How long the bleeding or symptoms have been going on
bpc.talk.2: Which medicines you have already taken from the pharmacy
bpc.talk.3: Why colonoscopy may be needed in your case
bpc.talk.4: Any other illness you have, or medicines you are currently on
bpc.talk.5: What the path after treatment and the follow-up will look like
bpc.talk.p: Asking questions is not a weakness — with the answers in hand you can move through tests and treatment with peace of mind.
bpc.close.p: Avoiding treatment out of fear of colonoscopy is the biggest risk of all. If you have symptoms, go to the doctor — ask questions; the doctor will decide whether a test is needed, and do not rely on pharmacy medicines.
